tasks.short: Set and approve a public offering price using valuation, market conditions and investor demand.

steps.what: Gather market quotes, comparable issues, issuer financials and investor indications.
Reconcile dates, currencies, security terms and comparable instruments in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Calculate valuation ranges and demand sensitivities in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Draft the pricing memo with scenario results, market context and uncertainties.

loop.input: Checked pricing scenarios and source-linked market commentary.
loop.output: Pricing memo with cited figures, assumptions and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Validate every figure against scenario outputs; analyst checks reasoning and omissions.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unresolved claims return to the analyst.
loop.why_not_simpler: Tables are deterministic; explaining changing market context requires bounded free-text drafting.

steps.what: Discuss demand and issuer objectives, then agree a proposed offering price.
Approve the offering price, conditions and release deadline.
Send approved offering terms to syndicate participants through the {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: An integration on the {DATA_PLATFORM} reconciles licensed market data from the {OTHER}, issuer records from the {DOCS} and demand from the {CRM}, then runs versioned pricing calculations. A bounded drafting loop prepares the memo in the {DOCS}; the {WORKFLOW} records committee approval and releases only the exact approved terms through the {EMAIL} before their expiry.
tasks.previous_blocker: Market-data rights, inconsistent security identifiers and bespoke deal assumptions made reliable connections expensive. Price accountability also discouraged separating calculations from approval.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building connectors, reconciliation rules and reusable calculation templates. Existing numerical methods remain the foundation.
tasks.still_hard: Thin markets, unreliable demand indications and changing conditions require judgement. Data licensing and deal-specific instruments can dominate implementation cost.
tasks.human_edge: Read investor intent, weigh issuer priorities and accept responsibility for pricing under uncertainty.

ambition.what: Intraday repricing reviews triggered by material changes in investor demand.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time assembling price packs and more time challenging demand and assumptions. They can initiate repricing reviews; final pricing authority remains with the pricing committee.

reach.task: Assess downside exposure across alternative offering prices.
reach.learn: Liquidity stress, concentration limits and scenario interpretation.

evidence.claim: Deterministic calculations can generate pricing scenarios; selecting a public offering price still requires accountable judgement.
Moody's Credit Memo drafts financial narratives from structured analysis and deal documents; this supports the memo pattern, not securities pricing.
The digest's financial-model benchmark illustrates why numerical outputs need independent tie-outs.

assumptions: This task occurs in a specialist capital-markets team; many mid-size companies do not perform it.
The first build covers one instrument family and established pricing methods.
Time shares and remaining effort are estimates; preparation takes substantial time despite judgement dominating accountability.
The release policy permits automatic distribution of unchanged, approved terms before a defined expiry.
Build ranges are working-day estimates, not measured outcomes.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply where relevant; national rules govern any employee consultation required by the deployment.
unknowns: Which instruments, markets and approval mandates are in scope?
Are market-data licences compatible with automated processing and derived outputs?
Can investor indications be exported with reliable timestamps and identifiers?
Which access, retention and national consultation requirements apply?
research_questions: Which identifier and timestamp checks detect stale or incomparable pricing inputs?
What independent calculation best validates each supported instrument?
What events must invalidate an approved release?
new_work: Resolve stale quotes, identifier mismatches and missing terms.
Review memo claims and pricing assumptions.
Maintain instrument templates, numerical checks and release rules.
Review connector permissions and market-data licence changes.

tasks.short: Build client trust, understand financial needs and follow through on agreed actions.

steps.what: Review client history, holdings and open issues before contact.

loop.input: Permission-filtered client history, portfolio facts and open actions.
loop.output: Source-linked briefing with outstanding commitments and suggested questions.
loop.check: Match portfolio facts to source records; analyst checks context and unsupported inferences.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; missing records remain explicit.
loop.why_not_simpler: Client correspondence contains contextual concerns that fixed field summaries miss.

steps.what: Arrange a suitable meeting through the {EMAIL} and {CALENDAR}.
Discuss goals, explain trade-offs and agree next actions with the client.
Record client preferences, decisions and action owners in the {CRM}.

loop.input: Analyst's meeting notes and agreed actions.
loop.output: Proposed record changes, action owners and due dates.
loop.check: Validate record IDs and dates; analyst confirms commitments before saving.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass; ambiguous commitments require manual entry.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text notes do not consistently separate preferences, decisions and commitments.

steps.what: Write and send a personal follow-up confirming agreed actions.

loop.input: Confirmed meeting outcomes, actions and approved supporting material.
loop.output: Personal follow-up ready for analyst approval.
loop.check: Check commitments against the client record; analyst approves wording, recipient and attachments.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; disputed advice or new commitments return to the analyst.
loop.why_not_simpler: Sensitive explanations and relationship context need tailored language beyond a fixed confirmation template.

steps.what: Check action deadlines and remind colleagues through the {CRM}.

tasks.design: Configure scheduling, action ownership and reminders in the {CALENDAR} and {CRM}. Bounded loops assemble source-linked briefings and propose records and follow-ups; the analyst leads conversations, approves record changes and approves each personal message before the {EMAIL} sends it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Client context was scattered across correspondence and records. Recording commitments and writing useful follow-ups required repeated reading and manual entry.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing scheduling and reminder features handle coordination. Bounded language processing can turn permitted notes and correspondence into reviewable drafts.
tasks.still_hard: Trust, difficult conversations and changes in client intent remain human work. Incomplete history limits briefing quality.
tasks.human_edge: Notice hesitation, explain uncertainty honestly and make commitments the client can trust.

ambition.what: A quarterly financial-goals check-in for smaller existing client accounts.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends more of the week in prepared client conversations and less on coordination. They can prioritise proactive check-ins within agreed service rules; authority to make financial commitments does not expand.

reach.task: Plan client service capacity around unresolved needs and commitments.
reach.learn: Service economics, escalation thresholds and workload planning.

evidence.claim: Scheduling, action ownership and reminders can use existing records and calendar configuration.
Bounded briefing and follow-up drafting can reduce preparation work, but relationship outcomes remain uncertain.

assumptions: This is a client-facing analyst role; an internal corporate analyst would serve internal stakeholders instead.
The investment-record category is represented by the {OTHER}.
The workflow uses analyst notes and does not require meeting recordings.
Conversation takes the largest time share; the supplied means priors understate it for ongoing relationship work.
Build ranges and remaining effort are estimates for one team.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply where relevant; national rules determine employee consultation obligations.
unknowns: Which client records and correspondence may be processed for this purpose?
Are client preferences and action owners reliably recorded?
What communications require additional review under the firm's service policy?
Does released capacity support a quarterly service for smaller accounts?
research_questions: Which briefing omissions most often cause poor client conversations?
Can extracted commitments be distinguished reliably from tentative discussion?
Which existing scheduling and reminder features already meet the need?
new_work: Check briefing sources and remove unsupported interpretations.
Approve extracted commitments and personal follow-ups.
Resolve duplicate client records and stale action owners.
Maintain access filters, drafting instructions and reminder rules.

tasks.short: Create accurate charts from financial data and insert them into technical reports.

steps.what: Export the required financial data from the {ERP} or investment-record system in the {OTHER}.
Clean categories, align periods and calculate chart measures in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Choose chart forms and format series, labels and axes in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Verify figures, scales, comparability and the message conveyed by each chart.
Insert checked charts and source notes into the report in the {DOCS}.

tasks.design: A scheduled integration on the {DATA_PLATFORM} builds validated chart datasets from the {ERP} and {OTHER}. Configured templates in the {SPREADSHEET} generate charts, while a deterministic generator inserts analyst-checked charts and source notes into report drafts in the {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Inconsistent exports, changing category names and manual report insertion made refreshes fragile. Existing chart templates were often disconnected from validated data.
tasks.enabler_now: Standard chart features already cover recurring reports. AI-assisted coding makes source mappings, validation rules and document insertion cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: A technically correct chart can still mislead through its scale, comparison or omitted context. Unusual analytical questions need fresh design choices.
tasks.human_edge: Choose the comparison that helps the reader understand the financial issue and notice misleading presentation.

ambition.what: An accessible chart appendix with underlying data for each recurring technical report.

tasks.altitude: The analyst reviews exceptions and visual meaning instead of repeatedly formatting charts. They can improve comparison choices and accessibility; report publication authority stays with the report owner.

reach.task: Define reusable financial measures and chart conventions.
reach.learn: Metric governance, accessible visual design and dataset versioning.

evidence.claim: Recurring charts can be generated through configured templates and deterministic data transformations without a language model.
The digest's numerical benchmark supports independent checks rather than trusting model-generated financial arithmetic.

assumptions: Most work concerns recurring chart families with agreed metric definitions.
Configuration handles common chart choices; the analyst reviews unfamiliar comparisons.
The supplied high automation prior fits routine production better than the final choice of analytical message.
Insertion produces an internal report draft; external publication is outside this task.
Build ranges and remaining effort are estimates for one report family.
GDPR applies to personal data; EU AI Act obligations depend on any AI actually deployed. National consultation rules apply where relevant.
unknowns: Which reports, chart families and export formats recur?
Are metric definitions and source totals agreed?
Does the existing {SPREADSHEET} support the required reusable templates?
What accessibility and publication standards must reports meet?
Which access and national consultation requirements apply?
research_questions: Which transformations can be replaced by existing source-system reporting configuration?
Which automatic checks best detect misleading scales and incompatible periods?
Can report insertion preserve readable labels and source notes across output formats?
new_work: Resolve failed data checks and unfamiliar categories.
Review chart meaning, readability and accessibility.
Maintain metric mappings, chart templates and report insertion rules.

tasks.short: Model financial alternatives and assess how transactions affect value, cash and capital.

steps.what: Agree the financial question, alternatives, constraints and decision criteria with the sponsor.
Gather historical financials, forecasts and transaction terms from the {ERP} and {DOCS}.
Reconcile inputs and document assumptions in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Adapt model formulas and run base, downside and alternative transaction scenarios.
Independently check model logic, source tie-outs and sensitivity behaviour.
Write the financial impact memo and discuss trade-offs with the decision sponsor.

loop.input: Validated scenario results, assumptions, limitations and decision criteria.
loop.output: Draft impact memo with source-linked figures and explicit trade-offs.
loop.check: Match every figure to validated results; analyst determines the recommendation and explains limitations.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unresolved interpretation remains with the analyst.
loop.why_not_simpler: Tables and standard disclosures are deterministic; case-specific explanation needs bounded language drafting.

tasks.design: A versioned calculation service on the {DATA_PLATFORM} connects {ERP} exports and structured assumptions, generates financial scenarios and returns reviewable models to the {SPREADSHEET}. Deterministic checks support independent review, then a bounded loop drafts a source-linked impact memo in the {DOCS}; the analyst frames the recommendation and the sponsor retains transaction authority.
tasks.previous_blocker: Bespoke transaction structures and workbook dependencies made reuse difficult. Teams lacked consistent input contracts, model versions and independent checks.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of implementing tested calculation modules, scenario runners and report generators. Financial mathematics and review disciplines remain established methods.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing model boundaries, forecasting behaviour and interpreting unusual transactions remain judgement-heavy. Novel structures may require substantial specialist work.
tasks.human_edge: Ask whether the model answers the right question, challenge assumptions and explain where apparent precision conceals uncertainty.

ambition.what: A weekly capital-allocation review using refreshed downside scenarios.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends more time comparing alternatives and challenging assumptions, with less workbook construction. They can propose additional scenarios and recommend deferral; investment approval rights remain with the sponsor.

reach.task: Translate transaction scenarios into funding and forecast changes.
reach.learn: Budget baselines, cash phasing and forecast reconciliation.

reach.task: Challenge downside assumptions and model limitations.
reach.learn: Stress design, correlated risks and independent model validation.

evidence.claim: Established model families can use deterministic calculation modules; problem framing and novel transaction logic still require analysts.
DataSnipper supports evidence extraction and financial checks with human review; it is an adjacent validation capability.
Baker Tilly Netherlands reported statement checking falling from eight to two hours; this is a vendor-reported adjacent case, not a modelling result.
The digest reports a cash-waterfall benchmark error, supporting independent numerical validation.

assumptions: The first build supports established valuation and transaction model families rather than arbitrary new instruments.
Transaction terms are supplied as structured fields; interpreting unusual legal clauses remains specialist work.
The supplied automation prior fits repeated calculations; framing, assumption selection and validation retain material human effort.
Independent review is available before results support a material decision.
Build ranges and remaining effort are estimates for the initial model families.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply where relevant; national rules determine any employee consultation obligations.
unknowns: Which model families and transaction structures recur?
Are model specifications, assumptions and source records versioned?
Which materiality thresholds require independent review?
Who can approve model changes and transaction recommendations?
Which access and national consultation requirements apply?
research_questions: Which reference calculations and financial identities can independently validate each model family?
How should scenario inputs expose uncertainty without suggesting false precision?
Which model changes require specialist revalidation rather than routine regression checks?
new_work: Maintain calculation modules, reference cases and model versions.
Resolve source reconciliation failures and unsupported transaction structures.
Review assumptions, scenario coverage and model limitations.
Check drafted explanations against validated numerical results.

role.altitude: The analyst's week shifts toward framing decisions, challenging assumptions and explaining uncertainty. Faster preparation supports more frequent reviews, while pricing, investment and client commitment rights remain with their designated decision makers.
reach: Financial Risk Specialist: stress-test pricing and capital decisions.
Budget Analyst: connect transaction scenarios to forecasts and funding.
Business Intelligence Analyst: establish reusable financial measures and reporting conventions.
Financial Manager: plan service capacity and capital-allocation reviews.
skills_to_grow: Financial model specification and independent validation.
Data lineage, reconciliation and access-aware integration.
Scenario design and communication of uncertainty.
Client listening and explanation of financial trade-offs.
Review of source-linked drafts and exception handling.
role.ambitious_version: Provide a recurring decision service that connects current financial data, validated scenarios and human advice, giving sponsors and clients earlier opportunities to reconsider financial choices.
